claim: A fireball erupts from a point, a turbulent ball of flame expanding and rolling outward through depth before fading to smoke — looping.

q1_defects.answer: Yes, multiple. The effect is almost entirely dark: after the first frame it collapses to a near-black smudge. play-2 and play-3 are essentially empty (meanLuma ~8 of 255), so for most of the loop there is nothing to see. The 'scale' control sweep produces no visible change between its low and high positions. Slab/seam stepping is also visible as blocky shelves in the smoke body.
evidence: metrics: play-2 meanLuma=8.1, play-3 meanLuma=7.9 (near-black; play-1 was 25)
metrics: control scale changed=false; control-scale-low vs control-scale-high visually identical

q2_reads_as.answer: No — it does not read as fire. The brightest frames (idle, play-1) show a desaturated pink/lavender smoke ball with a pale cream-blue core, like a dusty nebula or a moon lit from inside, not flame. The dominant hue is blue/violet, not fire's warm band. The ground-truth fire-flame/play-2.png is unmistakable orange/amber flame; this tile shares none of that warmth.
evidence: metrics: play-2 effHue=231 (blue), coolFrac=1.0, warmFrac=0 -> 100% cool, not fire
metrics: play-1 effHue=358 effSat=0.18 (washed pink-red, low sat) vs fire band 10-45 deg high sat
fire-flame/ground-truth/play-2.png : bright orange/amber flame for comparison

q3_discoverable.answer: Partly. The labeled Burst Rate control does change the frame (burstRate changed=true), so a user sweeping it sees something move. But the 'scale' control is dead, so a user who tries it would be confused when nothing happens.

q4_responsive.answer: Janky/dead for most of the loop. play-1 to play-2 changes (frameDeltaMag=19.37) but play-2 to play-3 is frozen (frameDeltaMag=0.18) AND both are near-black, so the loop spends most of its time showing essentially nothing rather than a rolling, expanding fireball.

q5_net.answer: A user would be annoyed: it is supposed to be an erupting ball of flame, and instead they get a dim pinkish-blue smoke puff that goes black for most of the loop and never looks like fire.

mustFix.issue: Does not read as fire — dominant hue is blue/violet (cool), not fire's warm band; brightest frame is a washed pink-cream smoke ball, not flame.
Effect collapses to near-black for most of the loop — no visible fireball during play-2/play-3.
The 'scale' control does nothing across its full range.
mustFix.evidence: fireball-burst/before/control-scale-high.png : metrics control scale changed=false (low and high identical)

flags.note: Blocky slab/seam stepping visible in the smoke body of the brighter frames.
